title: Two computable arrays of Turing indexes: a colouring from the k-th jump whose thin sets compute the k-th jump
source_title: Ramsey-like theorems for the Schreier barrier

standard_prerequisites.name: Thin sets, uniform moduli of a jump and computation from a set
standard_prerequisites.statement: A set is thin for a colouring of finite tuples in a colour when no tuple of the set of the relevant length has that colour; a uniform modulus of a set is a function that dominates every function computed by that set; and a set computes another when the latter is decidable relative to the former, written with the usual Turing-reduction symbol. The author's own notation is retained inside the counted statement and proof.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is the engine of the section: it produces both the colouring lived on the k-th jump and the indexes that turn any infinite thin set back into the k-th jump, and the following results of the section are built on exactly those two arrays.

core_obligations: Uniformly compute, for each positive k, an index for a uniform modulus of the k-th jump, which is possible because the k-th jump is a delta-complete set at the appropriate level, and note that the indexes can be found uniformly in k (source line 688).

Define the colouring for n at least two: on a tuple look at the value of the modulus at the smallest entry and compare it with the second entry; return the largest colour below n minus one whose associated entry still sits below the modulus value, and return n minus one when the second entry is already at least the modulus value (source line 690).

Rule out the top colour for an infinite thin set: given any smallest entry of the set there are further entries of the set beyond the modulus value at that entry, so a tuple of the required length takes the top colour, which would contradict thinness for the top colour (source line 692).

Rule out the next colour and then all remaining colours by contradiction: a tuple taking colour n minus two with the modulus value above its last entry can be extended, using the colours already excluded, to a tuple taking the colour c that the set was assumed thin for, and iterating the argument excludes every colour below n minus one as well (source line 694).

Read the computation off the thinning property: writing the set in increasing order, the modulus value at each element is bounded by the element n minus one places later, so the set computes a function dominating the modulus, hence computes the k-th jump, uniformly in the set, k and n (source line 696).

proof_roadmap.step: Uniform indexes for a modulus of the k-th jump.
Definition of the colouring by comparison with the modulus value at the smallest entry.
The top colour cannot occur on an infinite thin set.
Colour n minus two, and then every lower colour, is excluded by extending a tuple past the modulus value.
The thinning property bounds the modulus along the set, so the set computes the k-th jump.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2412.11598v3 的 Lemma lem:arrays（源 683-685 行，证明 687-697 行）：存在两个**可计算**的图灵指数阵列 (e_{n,k})、(d_{n,k})，使对 n≥2，Φ^{∅^(k)}_{e_{n,k}} 是着色 f_n^k:[N]^n→n，且每个无穷 f_n^k-thin 集 H 满足 Φ^H_{d_{n,k}} = ∅^(k)。关键操作不是例行核验：先要**一致地**为每个 k 得到 ∅^(k) 的一致模数 g_k 的 Δ^0_{k+1}-指数（688 行），再按「看最小元处的 g_k 值与第二个元的比较」显式定义着色（690 行），然后分三步排除颜色：顶色 n−1 不可能（692 行）、次色 n−2 不可能（694 行），而 694 行那一步必须用已排除的颜色把元组续长到任意给定色 c 从而矛盾；最后把 thin 性翻译成 g_k(x_i) ≤ x_{i+n−1} 的界，得到 H 计算 ∅^(k) 且一致（696 行）。难点在于「一致可计算」与「按颜色逐个排除」两条要求同时满足，且末步要把组合界的论证写成一致性陈述；原文位置在证明的 688、690、692、694、696 行。

editorial_notes: The counted unit is the article's own Lemma lem:arrays at source lines 683-685 together with its proof at source lines 687-697, a straight adjacent pairing in the pinned file. The pinned file is a concatenation of the authors' main and macro files; it is the article's fixed version arXiv:2412.11598v3 under CC BY 4.0.

This source ships no separate preamble file, so the retained preamble is sliced mechanically from the pinned file by the lane and is shared, byte for byte, with the other cards of this source; it carries the authors' full macro block so that no macro of a retained span is left undefined. The first card of this source needed one revision for exactly that reason.

The retained statement and proof contain no reference to another labelled result of the article and no citation, so this card carries no navigation pointer and no bibliography entry. The two arrays produced by the lemma are used by later results of the article, and those results are counted by other lanes; none of them is reproduced here.

The proof's final sentence is a uniformity claim about the computation it has just built, and it is part of the author's own argument rather than a pointer to another result, so it is retained verbatim.
